latest.question: Deputy Peadar Tóibín asked the Minister for Transport to detail the governance, procurement, audit and accountability structures that will be in place for MetroLink; the frequency with which cost and schedule performance will be reviewed; the thresholds that will trigger Ministerial intervention; and the mechanisms that will be used to prevent cost overruns and protect public funds throughout the project lifecycle.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 89, 97 and 99 together.
As the Deputy may be aware, significant progress has been made recently in moving MetroLink towards the construction phase. There has been, and will continue to be, appropriate oversight arrangements in place as part of this development.
Under the Infrastructure Guidelines, the Government provided "Approval Gate 2" consent for MetroLink on 16th September 2026. MetroLink may now proceed to the detailed procurement phase for the key contracts, with the main tender packs expected to issue to the market in the first half of next year and heavy construction anticipated to commence in 2028. Before MetroLink may commence these heavy construction works, the Government's approval will be required at Approval Gate 3 of the Infrastructure Guidelines.
Furthermore, on 16th June 2026, the Government approved the drafting of the MetroLink Bill 2026, in line with the General Scheme which I presented to Cabinet. This Bill will establish the Statutory Delivery Body charged with overseeing MetroLink through construction. The Statutory Delivery Body will be responsible for delivering MetroLink on budget and on time, and its Board and CEO will be fully accountable to the Minister for Transport and to the Oireachtas. The Body is expected to be subject to audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General, which publishes reports on its findings. Legislative drafters from the Office of Parliamentary Counsel to the Government are currently drafting

latest.question: Deputy Peadar Tóibín asked the Minister for Transport if a maximum budget ceiling has been established for MetroLink contracts; and the mechanisms that will be used to prevent costs exceeding approved budgets.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 98 and 100 together.
MetroLink is Ireland's largest public transport infrastructure project and a key National Development Plan priority, delivering long-term benefits for economic growth, housing competitiveness and climate action. MetroLink will provide a high-capacity, fully automated metro connection Dublin airport with key destinations across the city, including a reliable 25-minute journey to the city centre.
Over the last year, significant progress has been made in moving MetroLink from planning and design and into procurement and construction.
As the Deputy will be aware, An Coimisiún Pleanála published its decision to grant the MetroLink Railway Order, or planning permission, in October 2025. Following the resolution of a subsequent legal challenge, MetroLink secured an Operative Railway Order in January 2026. This enabled Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) to commence the shortlisting process for major MetroLink contracts.
In February, TII published the contract notice and Pre-Qualification Questionnaires (PQQ) for the two heavy civil works contracts, M401 and M402. The maximum combined contract value stated in the contract notice for these PQQs is €7.9 billion, excluding VAT.

latest.question: Deputy Aidan Farrelly asked the Minister for Transport if he will provide an update on the development of legislative changes to the Taxi Regulation Act 2013 with respect to cross-Border taxi services.
latest.reply:
I propose to take Questions Nos. 92 and 96 together.
The regulation of the small public service vehicle (SPSV) industry is a matter for the independent transport regulator, the National Transport Authority (NTA), under the provisions of the Consolidated Taxi Regulation Acts 2013 and 2016. Under section 6(2) of this Act, An Garda Síochána is responsible for the granting of SPSV driver licences. I have no role in the day-to-day operations of the SPSV sector.
Under the provisions of the Taxi Regulation Act 2013, operators are required to hold an SPSV licence and an SPSV driver licence to carry persons for hire or reward in the State. The 2013 Act and its requirements only apply to services provided in the State - it does not provide for services across a border. The legislative position in Northern Ireland is similar. Thus, under current legislation, a taxi operator wishing to operate cross-border services, would have to apply for and obtain SPSV licences on each side of the border. Unlike other areas of transport - such as bus and road haulage operations - taxi services are not subject to EU harmonisation, so arrangements for regulating taxi services remain a matter for the relevant authorities in each EU Member State, in respect of services that operate in their jurisdiction.

latest.question: Deputy Ciarán Ahern asked the Minister for Transport whether the evaluation process under condition 10 of the Dublin airport north runway planning permission (details supplied) is genuinely assessing the effectiveness of the property buy-out scheme as mitigation, including whether it enables affected households to relocate without being disadvantaged.
latest.reply:
In 2007, planning permission was granted for the development of Dublin Airport's North Runway, subject to 31 conditions. Condition 9 required the provision of a Voluntary Dwelling Purchase Scheme (VDPS) to facilitate the voluntary acquisition of qualifying residential properties.
Under the terms of the VDPS, once a fair valuation price is agreed through the process, daa pays an additional premium of 30% on the agreed price. It is open to homeowners to have their property independently evaluated at daa’s expense and daa will also cover the cost of conveyancing fees, stamp duty, tax advice and moving costs.
Condition 10 of the planning permission further requires that the VDPS be reviewed biannually, to ensure its continued effectiveness and appropriateness:
“Noise and flight track monitoring shall be operated at all times as detailed in the Environmental Impact Statement Addendum received by the planning authority on the 9th day of August, 2005 and in accordance with the recommendations of ECAC.CEAC.Doc 29. An annual report on noise contours shall be submitted to the planning authority. A noise and flight track monitoring report shall be submitted to the planning authority on a quarterly basis and shall be made available for public inspection. latest.question: Deputy Michael Healy-Rae asked the Minister for Transport when an RTSS scheme payment will be made to a haulier (details supplied).
latest.reply:
My Department received over 4,400 applications, in respect of approximately 31,500 vehicles. As of 06 October 2026, all applications received during the original application window have been assessed and approved for payment.
The applicant whose details you have shared with me provided the incorrect email address on their application. An official from my Department made contact with the applicant by phone and gathered corrected contact information for the applicant.
The applicant was advised that other information provided on their application was invalid and was provided a link to the application portal to correct their application. Unfortunately, the applicant did not provide the updated information necessary to process their application. As a result, the applicant will need to submit an appeal under the appeals process.
If the applicant provides the necessary information required to accurately and fairly assess their application during the appeals process, officials in my Department can then process their application.

latest.question: Deputy Ivana Bacik asked the Minister for Transport the position regarding so-called rickshaw vehicles carrying passengers for monetary reward; the adequacy of measures to enforce a ban on motorised rickshaws announced in 2018; the number of enforcements taken against operators of mechanically propelled rickshaws carrying passengers for reward under existing SPSV legislation in each year since 2016, in tabular form; his plans to further review guidance to An Garda Síochána or new legislation, following recent road traffic incidents involving rickshaws.
latest.reply:
For the Deputy's information, if a rickshaw is fitted with a small engine or electric motor of any kind, it is considered to be a mechanically propelled vehicle (MPV). Under road traffic law, if an MPV is used in a public place it is subject to all of the regulatory controls that apply to other vehicles i.e., it must be roadworthy, registered, taxed and comply with the following regulations:
• SI 190 of 1963 – Road Traffic Construction, Equipment and Use of Vehicles Regulations 1963.
• SI 189 of 1963 – Road Traffic Lighting of Vehicles Regulations 1963.
• SI 5 of 2003 – Road Traffic Construction and Use of Vehicles Regulations 2003.
The drivers of all vehicles on public roads, including motorised rickshaws, are required to comply with road traffic legislation and to behave in a safe manner paying due care to other road users. The enforcement of such road traffic legislation is a matter for An Garda Síochána. Therefore, statistics on the number of enforcement actions taken against operators of mechanically propelled rickshaws, would be a matter for An Garda Síochána.
A provision was contained in section 31 of the Road Traffic Act 2016, which was aimed at amending section 20 of the Taxi Regulation Act 2013, to allow the National Transport Authority (NTA) to make regulations for “non-motorised passenger transport” in towns and cities which includes rickshaws propelled by pedal cycle. latest.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Transport whether he plans to review the vehicle price ceiling under the SEAI electric vehicle purchase grant scheme; whether a tapered reduction in grant assistance above the ceiling has been assessed as an alternative to the immediate loss of eligibility.
latest.reply:
The Government is fully committed to supporting the transition to zero-emission and the ambitious target to have 30% of private car fleet switched to electric by 2030.
Regarding the EV Purchase Grant, the maximum eligible vehicle price threshold for the grant will now be €50,000, rather than €60,000. This change has been made to target funding for EV transition towards lower price bracket cars and enables a greater proportion of the funding available within the National Development Plan to support the roll-out of charging infrastructure. The amended price threshold came into place for new applications received after 31 July 2026, and will be kept under review in 2027.
The EV grant system is continually reviewed to optimise EV purchasing with a view to replacing older, polluting vehicles. It should be noted that decisions on financial incentives, including EV grants, must be taken in the context of overall financial sustainability.

latest.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Transport whether his Department has assessed the extent to which existing electric vehicle incentives meet the practical needs of larger families and households requiring greater range, passenger capacity, boot space or towing capability; whether this assessment will inform future changes to the scheme.
latest.reply:
The Government is fully committed to supporting the transition to zero-emission and the ambitious target to have 30% of private car fleet switched to electric by 2030.
In 2026, €170m has been allocated to support Ireland’s continued transition to Electric Vehicles (EV’s) including funding for EV purchase grants and home charger grants, and development of publicly available EV charging infrastructure.
Current incentives provided by the Department of Transport to support drivers' transition to electric include:
• a €3,500 purchase grant for battery electric vehicles (BEVs) up to €50,000 in value
• a pilot scrappage scheme, ICE2EV
• a home charging grant scheme
• an apartment charging scheme
• benefit-in-kind tax relief for BEVs
• VRT relief of up to €5,000 for BEVs and
• a low rate of annual motor tax.
It should also be noted that the cost of EVs in all market segments is beginning to reduce as the market matures and manufacturers expand their offerings. In addition, EVs can offer significantly lower running costs than conventional petrol or diesel vehicles.
The EV grant system is continually reviewed to optimise EV purchasing with a view to replacing older, polluting vehicles. It should be noted that decisions on financial incentives, including EV grants, must be taken in the context of overall financial sustainability.

latest.question: Deputy Michael Healy-Rae asked the Minister for Transport if the local link service travelling from Ardgroom in County Cork will travel earlier to make connecting services in Kenmare and Killarney in order to allow persons to arrive in Cork earlier to start work, attend college and so on.
latest.reply:
As Minister of State at the Department of Transport with special responsibility for Rural Transport, I have responsibility for policy and overall funding in relation to rural public transport service provision; however, I am not involved in the day-to-day operations.
The National Transport Authority (NTA) has statutory responsibility for securing the provision of public passenger transport services nationally including Smart DRT pilots. In light of the NTA responsibilities I have referred your question to the NTA for direct reply to you. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within ten working days.

examples.question: Deputy Paul McAuliffe asked the Minister for Social Protection the eligibility of a person (details supplied) for a pension (non-contributory).
examples.reply:
An application for State pension non-contributory was received from the person concerned on 10 September 2024.
The maximum weekly rate of pension was awarded with effect from 19 September 2024 and notification of the decision issued, in writing, on 16 September 2024.
I hope this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Emer Currie asked the Minister for Education and Youth the position regarding a project (details supplied).
examples.reply:
As previously advised to the Deputy, the school referred to was approved to enter my Department's pipeline of projects under the Additional School Accommodation (ASA) scheme.
The project received approval from my Department to commence construction in January 2026. More recently, Department officials were notified by the school authorities that construction has now commenced. Expected completion to coincide with the start of the new school year.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Donnelly asked the Minister for Defence if she is aware of Irish Defence Forces members participating in military competitions with the Israeli Defence Forces; and if confirmed, her views on such on participation.
examples.reply:
The Defence Forces participate in international military competitions in order to promote in the Defence Forces the adoption of international best practice, exchange of tactics, techniques and procedures (TTP) and encourage the development of military skills. It also contributes to the development of particular military skillsets and doctrines.
The decision on who to invite to these competitions lies with the hosting nation. I am informed by the military authorities that the Defence Forces have not participated in any military competitions organised by the Israeli Defence Forces. I am also informed that, to date, no Defence Forces team has reported Israeli Defence Forces participation in competitions attended by Defence Forces personnel.

examples.question: Deputy Erin McGreehan asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine for an update on the timeline and commencement dates for the basic income support for sustainability scheme.
examples.reply:
My Department is fully committed to making payments to farmers under the various schemes at the earliest date possible and to the maximum number of farmers possible. This commitment to farmers is evidenced in the very high payment rates achieved across all schemes over the last number of years in both EU and Exchequer funded schemes.
The timelines for all schemes, including the planned payment dates, have been set after extensive consultation with farmers and taking account of application systems, monitoring systems, validation and processing systems and payment systems.
In 2025, my Department commenced payments under the Basic Income Support for Sustainability (BISS) scheme from October 16th ensuring money flowed as soon as practically possible to farmers.
This payment date is in line with the traditional payment date of the BISS Scheme to farmers and is as outlined in the Farmers' Charter.

examples.question: Deputy Tom Brabazon asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage for an update on the financial contribution scheme; and the rationale to no longer fund this scheme.
examples.reply:
The Government’s new housing plan, Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030, includes measures to increase delivery of housing for older people through increased delivery of social housing, increased delivery of more suitable homes in private housing and increased choice to support voluntary rightsizing, including a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes.
I understand that existing financial contribution schemes in place in some local authorities are non-statutory and therefore a matter for the individual local authorities. Consideration will be given to a review of the operation of existing local authority financial contribution schemes and my Department is advancing these measures now incorporated in the new housing plan.

examples.question: Deputy Réada Cronin asked the Minister for Climate, Energy and the Environment what specific regulatory changes are being sought by Re-Turn for the proposed rPET reprocessing facility; the Department's position on the establishment of such a processing facility.
examples.reply:
Re-turn is a producer-led and owned, not-for-profit company established by beverage producers to meet their obligations under the Separate Collection (Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations.
Re-turn has stated its ambition to develop an rPET reprocessing facility in Ireland. In this regard, Re-turn has briefed me and Departmental officials on its plans.
The matter remains under consideration, with the Department considering the various public policy considerations that arise.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Transport further to Parliamentary Question No.199 of 16 April 2026, regarding Ireland's current position (details supplied); whether he has articulated this position either internally with Irish officials or with European counterparts; if so, if he will provide details of what was articulated and through which medium.
examples.reply:
I am aware of the concerns raised by car rental fleet operators regarding the Clean Corporate Vehicles proposal. We engage regularly with representatives from this sector and have met with them several times over the past year, including discussions specifically on this proposal.
It should be noted that the measure remains at proposal stage, with negotiations currently underway at EU level. The Regulation will not be finalised until such time as an agreement is reached between the Council and the European Parliament. This process is expected to run through 2026, which intersects with Ireland’s Presidency of the Council of the EU.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Murphy asked the Minister for Agriculture, Food and the Marine the numerical, scientific and editorial verification carried out before the Wildlife Unit End of Year Report for 2025 that was approved for publication; whether further errors have since been identified; and whether his Department will publish an amended report clearly identifying all corrections.
examples.reply:
The Wildlife Report compiled by my Department has stated that there was 7,625 badger captures in the vaccine area in 2025. This is the correct figure. The figure of 8,123 is the number of badger captures that were recorded in vaccine areas for 2024. Table 4 in the report states the correct figures of badger captures for 2024 and 2025.
For the purposes of clarity the figure for 2024 will be removed from the body of the text.

examples.question: Deputy Carol Nolan asked the Minister for Social Protection the number of people who have had their receipt of jobseeker's allowance or jobseeker's benefit permanently withdrawn or revoked for breach of the conditions associated with their claim, and who have not subsequently had their claim reinstated, from January 2020 to date.
examples.reply:
To be eligible for a Jobseeker's payment a person must satisfy all the eligibility criteria for the relevant scheme.
Where a claim has been stopped, it will only be re-instated following an application by the customer and where all conditions of the scheme are satisfied.
It is not possible to provide data on the number of claims stopped and not subsequently re-instated due to the large churn on jobseekers schemes and the many legitimate reasons that claims are stopped.
I trust that this clarifies matters for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy Ruth Coppinger asked the Minister for Social Protection the annual figures since 2015 for appeals lodged with the social welfare appeals office querying a refusal based on the habitual residence condition, by Irish citizens and non-Irish nationals, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
I am advised by the Chief Appeals Officer that the Social Welfare Appeals Office does not collate data on appeals specifically relating to the Habitual Residence Condition, therefore the statistical information is not available.
I trust this clarifies the matter for the Deputy.

examples.question: Deputy John Paul O'Shea asked the Minister for Housing, Local Government and Heritage the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; and the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
examples.reply:
As the Valuation Tribunal is independent in the performance of its functions, my Department does not hold the information requested in relation to the number of appeals involving the rating of agricultural or horticultural buildings have been brought before the Valuation Tribunal since 2020; the number that were successful; or the average length of time taken to determine these appeals.
It is noted that certain information on Valuation Tribunal appeals activity is included in the Tribunal's Annual Reports, available on the organisation's website at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/about-us/publications/.
Judgements of the Valuation Tribunal are also published and can be accessed on the Tribunal's website (at: www.valuationtribunal.ie/judgments/) under 'Name', 'Year', 'Property category' and 'Rating Authority'. It is noted that the Tribunal does not, however, include a specific category of appeal termed 'agriculture / horticultural'.
The Deputy may wish to contact the Tribunal directly in relation to the information sought by emailing info@valuationtribunal.ie.

examples.question: Deputy Pa Daly asked the Minister for Health the total number of GPs, and the number of GPs providing GMS services, in County Kerry, by local health area and per 10,000 population, at 1 December for each year from 2020 to 2025, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
As this is a service matter, I have asked the HSE to reply to the Deputy directly as soon as possible.
Please note that as GPs are private practitioners, accordingly it may only be possible for the HSE to respond in relation to HSE contracted GPs.

examples.question: Deputy Paul Lawless asked the Minister for Transport for a record of all reported accidents, collisions, or safety incidents that have occurred at or in the vicinity of the unmarked traffic islands in Ballindine, County Mayo, on the N17, over the past 20 years; if road safety audits or assessments have been carried out at this location; and if there are plans to install appropriate road markings or safety measures at this site.
examples.reply:
As Minister for Transport, I have responsibility for overall policy and exchequer funding in relation to the National Roads Programme. Under the Roads Acts 1993-2015 and in line with the National Development Plan (NDP), the operation and management of individual national roads is a matter for Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII), in conjunction with the local authorities concerned. This is also subject to the Infrastructure Guidelines and the necessary statutory approvals. In this context, TII is best placed to advise you in relation to safety on the N17 at Ballindine, Co. Mayo.
The Government is committed to reducing road deaths and creating safer roads for everyone in Ireland.
Noting the above position, I have referred your question to TII for a direct reply. Please advise my private office if you do not receive a reply within 10 working days.

examples.question: Deputy Naoise Ó Muirí asked the Minister for Transport the payroll cost of his Department and of each organisation or agency under its remit individually, in 2015 to 2025, by year, in tabular form.
examples.reply:
The table below outlines the payroll costs of my Department from 2015-2025.

As this question also relates to agencies under the remit of the Department of Transport, I have referred the question to these agencies to reply to you directly. If the Deputy does not receive a response within ten working days, please contact my Private Office.
